slides.title: Leverage
slides.content: If you have $1,000, your broker might let you buy $2,000 worth of stock by lending you the other $1,000. This is called 'Buying on Margin'.

slides.title: Double Edged Sword
slides.content: If the stock goes up 10%, you made $200 on your $1,000 investment (a 20% gain!). But if it goes down 10%, you lost $200 (a 20% loss).

slides.title: The Margin Call
slides.content: If your stock drops too much, the broker gets nervous you can't pay them back. They will issue a 'Margin Call', forcing you to deposit cash immediately, or they will sell your stocks by force at a huge loss.

quiz.question: What does it mean to 'Buy on Margin'?

options.text: Buying a stock at the margin (edges) of the trading day
Borrowing money from your broker to buy more stock than you could normally afford
options.explanation: Margin is leverage provided by your broker.

options.text: Buying only the cheapest stocks available

quiz.question: What happens during a Margin Call?

options.text: The broker calls you to congratulate you on your profits
You must immediately deposit more cash or the broker will forcefully sell your stocks
options.explanation: The broker acts to protect their loaned money before your account goes negative.

options.text: You get a free stock from the broker
